newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES DEPRESSED IN LIQUID MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES DEPRESSED IN LIQUID MARKET.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were slightly depressed in early Tuesday trade, weighed down by improved liquidity following maturity of treasury bills worth Z$137.5 million, dealers said.
"It looks like the market is very liquid at the moment and the rates are depressed," one dealer said.

"The liquidity is due to some maturing treasury bills forecast at Z$137.5 million and we just had a treasury-bill auction call looking to raise Z$100 million from that which is likely to leave the market with a surplus," he said, adding results of the auction were not yet available.
The dealers said bankers acceptance bills were being bought at 16.75 percent and sold at 16.5 percent compared to 17.25 percent and 16.50 percent on Monday.

NCDs maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were changing hands at 17 percent and 16.75 percent (buying and selling respectively) versus 18 and 17 percent previously while the call rate slipped to 16.25 percent from 17.25 percent.
The central Reserve Bank indicated a market shortage of Z$4.7 million at Monday's close.
